# The AI-native ## A document representation built for how AI actually reads. Every component carries a semantic tag, bounding box coordinates, and reading order — natively encoded in a format LLM tokenizers can parse without translation overhead. A table encodes its full grid structure via OTSL. A heading carries its level and page position. ... The same standard extends beyond text documents. Audio transcripts, images, and video segments encode as first-class elements — speakers, timestamps, and scenes using the same primitives as headings and tables. What your parser returns ... J. Smith Q3 2024 Revenue $42M
## Six properties. No compromises. AI-native Every element maps directly to LLM tokens. No translation layers, no postprocessing, no structural guesswork. Lossless Tables keep their full grid structure. Figures keep their position. Reading order is preserved, not inferred. Expressive ... One canonical representation per content type. No parser-dependent variance. Every tool produces the same output. Open A Joint Development Foundation Projects standard and LF AI & Data project. Public spec, open working group, no lock-in. ... ## AI-native document format specification DocLang is a constrained XML format built from the ground up for LLM tokenizers — a 1-to-1 mapping between DocLang tokens and model tokens, with minimal token count. Every component carries semantic role, geometric bounding box, and reading order. Tables use OTSL: 5 structural tokens where HTML needs 28. PDF is a presentation format. It tells a renderer where to draw pixels. DocLang is a semantic format — it tells a model what content _is_ . # Optimized Table Tokenization for Table Structure Recognition
## Abstract
Since the token representation of the table structure has a significant impact on the accuracy and run-time performance of any Im2Seq model, we investigate in this paper how table-structure representation can be optimised. We propose a new, optimised table-structure language (OTSL) with a minimized vocabulary and specific rules.
The benefits of OTSL are that it reduces the number of tokens to 5 (HTML needs 28+) and shortens the sequence length to half of HTML on average. Consequently, model accuracy improves significantly, inference time is halved compared to HTML-based models, and the predicted table structures are always syntactically correct.

...

## Introduction
Their work introduces an Optimized Table Structure Language (OTSL) that demonstrates how thoughtful data representation design can significantly improve both model performance and efficiency.

...

## The Optimized Table Structure Language (OTSL)
To address these limitations, the authors propose OTSL, a purpose-built language for representing table structures in machine learning contexts. OTSL operates on a fundamentally different principle than HTML, using an atomic 2D grid representation where each cell position is explicitly defined.
**Core Vocabulary** : OTSL uses only 5 tokens:
* **C (cell)** : Represents a new, independent table cell
* **L (left-looking)** : Indicates horizontal merging with the left neighbor
* **U (up-looking)** : Indicates vertical merging with the upper neighbor
* **X (cross)** : Indicates merging with both left and upper neighbors
* **NL (new-line)** : Signals row transitions
**Syntactic Rules** : OTSL enforces six explicit rules that ensure backward-looking validation:
​ Left-looking rule: L must have ( L or C ) as left neighbor Up-looking rule: U must have ( U or C ) as upper neighbor Cross rule: X must have ( X or U ) left and ( X or L ) upper First row rule: Only C and L allowed in first row First column rule: Only C and U allowed in first column
Rectangular rule: All rows have equal token count ​ ​
These rules enable **immediate validation** of each predicted token by examining only preceding tokens, allowing for real-time error detection and correction during inference.

## Experimental Setup and Methodology
The authors integrated OTSL into TableFormer, a state-of-the-art transformer-based Im2Seq model. The experimental design involved:
**Datasets** : Three popular TSR datasets were used:
* PubTabNet (395k samples)
* FinTabNet (113k samples)
* PubTables-1M (~1M samples)
All datasets were converted from HTML to OTSL format, with converted versions to be publicly released.
**Evaluation Metrics** :

...

## Key Findings
**Performance Improvements** : OTSL consistently achieved comparable or superior accuracy while dramatically reducing inference time. On PubTabNet, OTSL achieved a TEDs of 0.955 (matching HTML) and mAP of 0.88 (vs. HTML's 0.857) while reducing inference time from 5.39 to 2.73 seconds - a 2x speedup.
**Model Efficiency** : OTSL enables the use of significantly smaller models while maintaining competitive performance. A 4-encoder, 2-decoder OTSL model achieved TEDs of 0.942 and mAP of 0.857 with only 1.22 seconds inference time, representing a 5-6x speedup compared to comparable HTML models.
**Generalization** : Results were consistent across all three datasets. On FinTabNet, OTSL showed superior performance (TEDs: 0.959 vs. 0.920, mAP: 0.862 vs. 0.722) while maintaining faster inference. Similar patterns emerged on PubTables-1M.

...

## Architectural Integration
The integration of OTSL into the TableFormer architecture demonstrates its compatibility with existing Im2Seq frameworks. The model processes table images through standardized image preprocessing, followed by encoder-decoder attention mechanisms that generate OTSL sequences.

...

## Comparative Analysis of Predictions
The detailed comparison reveals fundamental differences in how HTML and OTSL models handle complex table structures. The example shows a sparse table where HTML generates 258 tokens compared to OTSL's 135 tokens.

...

## Implications and Future Directions
The authors' commitment to releasing converted datasets in OTSL format will facilitate broader adoption and enable the research community to explore further optimizations and applications of this approach.

## Conclusion
The optimization of table structure representation through OTSL demonstrates that thoughtful data representation design can be as impactful as architectural innovations in deep learning.
By addressing fundamental limitations of HTML-based representations, OTSL achieves significant improvements in accuracy, efficiency, and reliability for table structure recognition tasks.

...

The main paper uses the TableFormer architecture as the basis for all of its experiments. It is selected as the state-of-the-art Image-to-Markup-Sequence model to directly compare the performance of the proposed OTSL representation against the standard HTML representation.

...

This paper introduced the PubTabNet dataset, which is the primary benchmark used for hyper-parameter optimization and evaluation in the main paper. It also helped popularize the use of HTML for table structure recognition, which is the specific representation the authors aim to improve upon with their OTSL.

...

This work introduced the FinTabNet dataset, one of the key public datasets used in the experiments to validate the effectiveness of the proposed OTSL representation. The authors show that their OTSL-trained model significantly outperforms an HTML-trained model on this specific dataset of financial tables.

...

This paper introduced the PubTables-1M dataset, a large-scale dataset used in the main paper's experiments to demonstrate the performance and scalability of the proposed OTSL method. The results on this dataset highlight that OTSL provides a distinct advantage over HTML when applied to a very large and diverse set of tables.

# Operational Technology Specifications Library (OTSL)
The OTSL gives requirements for Operational Technology products and services on motorways and all-purpose trunks roads, and related services.
Operational Technology Specifications Library (OTSL)
The OTSL replaces the historic Traffic Systems and Signing (TSS) Plans Registry and was launched in 2022.
It has inherited many of the TSS Plans Registry documents including specifications for equipment, and testing, as well as technical drawings and diagrams covering the following topic areas:
| Prefix | Description |
| MCE | Specifications for equipment. Also see 'TRs' |
| MCG | Specifications for testing. Also see 'TRGs' |
| MCL | Drawings, specifications, records, and maintenance manuals for lines and transmission systems. |
| MCS | Indices and lists |
| MCX | Standard installation drawings, cabinets, circuit diagrams, and printed circuit boards. |

...

The OTSL forms part of a larger suite of documents specifying design, construction and operational requirements for motorways and all-purpose trunk roads, namely the Design Manual for Roads and Bridges (DMRB) standards and Manual of Contract Documents for Highway Works (MCHW)

...

## How to access the OTSL
The documents contained within the OTSL include current versions of Operational Technology specifications as procured by National Highways, related forms, and supporting information documents which can all be download from the library.

...
